data.long_meaning: Nikhita is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Nikhat' which means 'to conquer' or 'to bring victory'. This name is deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and culture, symbolizing triumph over challenges and adversity. The name Nikhita carries the meaning “Victory Bringer” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nikhita usually hope their child will grow to embody victory bringer and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Nikhita was a celebrated Sanskrit scholar and commentator during the Gupta period (circa 5th century CE). He is known for his extensive commentary on Panini's Ashtadhyayi, a classic Sanskrit grammar text.

Another Nikhita, a Jain scholar from the 12th century CE, wrote a commentary on the Sutrakritanga, a foundational text of Jainism. His work, known as the 'Nikhilamrutasutra', is considered an important contribution to Jain scholarship.
